主要内容: Noble Group shareholders approved a $3.5 billion debt restructuring plan, which will result in them retaining only 20% ownership of the company, while granting majority control to a group of creditors, primarily hedge funds. The decision was made reluctantly due to the significant dilution of shareholder value. The crisis began in February 2015 when former employee Arnaud Vagner, under the pseudonym Iceberg Research, published reports accusing Noble of inflating its assets. This led to a share price collapse, credit downgrades, and asset sales. The restructuring plan aims to halve the company's debt and provide access to trade finance and hedging facilities. Noble's management will retain 10% ownership, while creditors will control 70%. The plan requires a simple majority of shareholders present at the meeting to pass. Noble's shareholders include China Investment Corp, Goldilocks Investment Co Ltd, and Eastspring Investments. Trading in Noble's shares was halted pending the announcement. Analysts note that Noble still faces challenges, with losses increasing to $128 million in the April to June quarter from $72 million in the first quarter.
